title: NSS feeds for Cloud & Branch Connector: limits, output and SIEM destination

prose.text: A feed is one connection from an NSS server to a SIEM for one log type. Its settings decide what is sent, in which format and to which address.

prose.label: Format.
prose.text: {{output-types}} {{timezone}} How a Session feed records sessions individually or in aggregates is in [[cloud-connector.logs.session-records]].

prose.label: Destination.
prose.text: {{siem-destination}} {{siem-rate}} Whether a feed can deliver to an HTTPS endpoint is open {{gap:https-destination}}.

prose.label: Gaps in delivery.
prose.text: {{duplicate-logs}} The buffer that covers a SIEM outage is in [[cloud-connector.nss-va.servers]].

prose.label: DNS feed defaults.
prose.text: {{dns-feed-defaults}} The HTTPS-push Cloud NSS feeds are in [[cloud-connector.nss-va.cloud-feeds]].

checks.do: How many feeds the server already carries, and how many of them are Session feeds, before adding one.

feed-limits.statement: Up to 16 NSS feeds can be added for each NSS, and Session logs are limited to 8 of them per NSS. Event log feeds can be configured up to 16.

quotes: You can add up to 16 NSS feeds for each NSS. (Session logs are limited to 8 feeds per NSS to ensure optimal performance.)
You can configure up to 16 Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) feeds to specify the data from the Event logs

per-feed-config.statement: Each feed can have its own list of fields, format and filters.

quotes: Each feed can have a different list of fields, a different format, and different filters.

output-types.statement: Feed output is a CSV list by default; Name Value Pairs, Tab Separated, JSON or Custom can be selected instead (stated in the Session and Event feed articles).

quotes: The output is a comma-separated value (CSV) list by default. You can select from Name Value Pairs, Tab Separated, JSON, or Custom if your SIEM accepts any of these formats.
The output is a comma-separated values (CSV) list by default. You can also select Custom, JSON, Name Value Pairs, or Tab Separated if your SIEM accepts any of these formats.

timezone.statement: A feed's time zone defaults to the organization's time zone and applies to the time field in the output; the configured time zone can also be output as a separate field.

quotes: By default, this is set to the organization's time zone. The time zone you set applies to the time field in the output file.
The configured time zone can be output to the logs as a separate field.

siem-destination.statement: A feed streams to a SIEM IP address or FQDN on a SIEM TCP port. With an FQDN the NSS re-resolves the name only when the existing connection goes down, which allows failover from one IP to another without relying on a DNS update, and the FQDN cannot be used for DNS-based load balancing.

quotes: SIEM Destination Type: The type of destination. Select from IP Address or FQDN.

SIEM FQDN: Enter the destination for the TCP connection to which the logs are streamed. This allows failover from one IP to the other without manual intervention, but without relying on updating the DNS entry.
The NSS re-resolves the FQDN only when the existing connection goes down. This feature cannot be used for DNS-based load balancing.
SIEM TCP Port: Enter the port number of the SIEM to which the logs are streamed.

siem-rate.statement: SIEM Rate is Unlimited by default; Limited caps the stream at a configured number of events per second, for SIEM licensing or other constraints.

quotes: The SIEM rate is set to Unlimited by default. Select Limited if you need to control the output stream due to SIEM licensing or other constraints.
SIEM Rate Limit (Events per Second)

duplicate-logs.statement: Duplicate Logs sets the number of minutes for which the NSS sends duplicate logs, so that no logs are skipped during downtime; in the Event feed article it is Disabled by default.

quotes: Duplicate Logs: To ensure that no logs are skipped during any downtime, specify the number of minutes that the NSS sends duplicate logs.
specify the number of minutes that the NSS sends duplicate logs. This is Disabled by default.

session-filters.statement: A Session feed can be filtered by policy action and rule name (both per the traffic forwarding rules), by location, Branch Connector group, Branch Connector and client IP address, by network service, and by gateway.

quotes: Policy Actions: Use this filter to limit the logs based on the action the service took, in accordance with the traffic forwarding rules.
Rule Name: Use this filter to limit the logs based on the configured traffic forwarding rule.
Locations: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific locations.
Branch Connector Groups: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific Branch Connector groups.
Branch Connector: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific Branch Connectors.
Client IP Addresses: Use this filter to limit the logs based on a client’s IP address.
Network Services: Select Any to apply the NSS feed to all network services
Gateway: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific gateways.

event-filters.statement: An Event feed can be filtered by location, by Cloud or Branch Connector group and by Cloud or Branch Connector VM.

quotes: Locations: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific locations.
Cloud/Branch Connector Groups: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific Cloud or Branch Connector groups.
Cloud/Branch Connector VM: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific Cloud or Branch Connector VMs.

dns-feed-limit.statement: Up to 16 NSS feeds can be configured for DNS logs.

quotes: You can configure up to 16 Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) feeds to specify the data from the DNS logs that the NSS sends to the security information and event management (SIEM) system.

metrics-feed-limit.statement: Up to 16 NSS feeds can be configured for Metrics logs.

quotes: You can configure up to 16 NSS feeds to specify the data from the Metrics logs that the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) sends to the security information and event management (SIEM) system.

dns-feed-filters.statement: A DNS feed filters by policy action, including Redirect to ZPA (limiting the logs to requests resolved with the IP pool), by rules in the DNS Control policy, by DNS responses (domain names, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and by session duration in seconds.

quotes: Redirect to ZPA: Use this filter to limit the logs to resolve DNS requests using the IP pool.
Rule Name: Use this filter to limit the logs based on specific rules in the DNS Control policy. Choose the rules from the list.
DNS Responses: Use this filter to limit the logs to sessions that contain specific data in the DNS responses. You can specify domain names, IPv4, and IPv6 addresses.
Durations: Use this filter to limit the logs based on the duration of the sessions, in seconds.

dns-feed-defaults.statement: On the DNS feed page the NSS type is NSS for Firewall, Cloud and Branch Connector by default and the status is Enabled by default; the output is a CSV list by default, with Custom, JSON, Name Value Pairs or Tab Separated selectable if the SIEM accepts them; and the setting for the number of minutes the NSS sends duplicate logs is Disabled by default.

quotes: NSS Type: The NSS type is set to NSS for Firewall, Cloud and Branch Connector by default.
Status: The status is Enabled by default.
The output is a comma-separated values (CSV) list by default. You can also select Custom, JSON, Name Value Pairs, or Tab Separated if your SIEM accepts any of these formats.
specify the number of minutes that the NSS sends duplicate logs. This is Disabled by default.

item-lists.statement: On the DNS feed page there is no limit on the number of locations that can be selected, and item lists show up to 500 items on a page.

quotes: There is no limit on the number of locations that you can select.

evidence.after: Client IP Addresses: Use this filter to limit the logs based on a client’s IP address. You can enter:
quotes: For item lists, you can view up to 500 items on a page;

metrics-feed.statement: A Metrics feed selects VM, Instance and/or Resource record types, where Instance metrics apply at an individual data processing instance level (there are multiple instances in a single Cloud or Branch Connector) and Resource metrics at an individual resource level (physical and logical resources used by all data processing instances); it can be limited to specific Cloud or Branch Connector VMs.

quotes: Metrics Record Type: Select VM, Instance, and/or Resource.
Instance: Metrics that are applicable at an individual data processing instance level. There are multiple data processing instances in a single Cloud or Branch Connector.
Resource: Metrics that are applicable at an individual resource level. There are physical and logical resources in a Cloud or Branch Connector that are used by all data processing instances.
Cloud/Branch Connector VM: Use this filter to limit the logs to specific Cloud or Branch Connector VMs.

cbc-guidelines.statement: The Cloud & Branch Connector general guidelines for NSS feeds recommend not including more than 50 fields in a feed to accommodate syslog message size limits, encode any URL character at or below 0x20, or equal to and above 0x7F, as %HH, say to use tabs as field delimiters, say field names are case-sensitive, and allow up to 16 NSS feeds for each NSS.

quotes: Zscaler recommends not including more than 50 fields in the NSS feed to accommodate syslog message size limits.
Any URL character that is less than or equal to 0x20, or equal to and above 0x7F, is encoded as %HH.
Use tabs as field delimiters.
Field names are case-sensitive.
You configure up to 16 NSS feeds for each NSS.

cbc-duplicate-example.statement: In the Cloud & Branch Connector page's example the SIEM went offline at 6:29:00 PM, the NSS detected the lost connection at 6:30:00 PM and the connection was restored at 6:40:00 PM; with Duplicate Logs set to 5 minutes the NSS resends the logs from 6:25:00 onward and sends 5 minutes of duplicate logs, with it disabled from 6:30:01 onward, and each log record has a unique ID stored in the recorded field that is used to discover duplicate logs.

quotes: For example, the SIEM went offline at 6:29:00 PM, the NSS detected the lost connection at 6:30:00 PM, and the connection was restored at 6:40:00 PM.
If Duplicate Logs is set to 5 minutes, the NSS resends the logs from 6:25:00 onward, after the connection is restored. It sends 5 minutes of duplicate logs.
If Duplicate Logs is disabled, the NSS resends the logs from 6:30:01 onward, after the connection is restored.
Each log record has a unique ID stored in the recorded field that is used to discover duplicate logs.

filter-cost.statement: A large number of filters, or complex filters such as string searches, can impact the performance of the NSS.

quotes: A large number of filters or complex filters, such as string searches, can impact the performance of the NSS.

duplicate-logs-example.summary: The Cloud & Branch Connector and ZIA general-guidelines pages give the same Duplicate Logs outage example (SIEM offline 6:29:00 PM, detected 6:30:00 PM, restored 6:40:00 PM) with different resend times and a different account of the duplicates.

quotes: If Duplicate Logs is disabled, the NSS resends the logs from 6:30:01 onward, after the connection is restored.
If Duplicate Logs is set to 5 minutes, the NSS resends the logs from 6:25:00 onward, after the connection is restored. It sends 5 minutes of duplicate logs.

positions.says: Disabled, the NSS resends from 6:30:01 onward; at 5 minutes it resends from 6:25:00 onward and sends 5 minutes of duplicate logs.

quotes: If Duplicate Logs is disabled: After the connection is restored, the NSS sends logs from 6:30:00 PM onwards. It does not recover logs from 6:29:00 PM to 6:30:00 PM.
It duplicates logs from 6:25:00 PM to 6:28:59 PM and recovers logs from 6:29:00 PM to 6:30:00 PM.

positions.says: Disabled, the NSS sends from 6:30:00 PM onwards and does not recover 6:29:00 to 6:30:00 PM; at 5 minutes it duplicates 6:25:00 to 6:28:59 PM and recovers 6:29:00 to 6:30:00 PM.

duplicate-logs-example.impact: Which logs a SIEM receives after an outage with Duplicate Logs disabled differs by one second between the pages, and for the 5-minute setting one page counts all 5 minutes as duplicates while the other splits them into 4 minutes duplicated and 1 minute recovered. The ZIA page's version is the claim shared.nss.reliability:duplicate-logs-example.

https-destination.title: Whether a Cloud & Branch Connector NSS feed can deliver to an HTTPS endpoint
https-destination.blocks: connecting an NSS VM to a SIEM that only exposes an HTTPS ingestion API
https-destination.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The NSS VA's raw TCP output cannot directly hit an HTTPS endpoint without a middleware adapter", with SIEM-specific guidance (Splunk raw TCP input on a heavy forwarder rather than HEC, ArcSight CEF over TCP, QRadar syslog TCP, Elastic Logstash TCP input). The Cloud & Branch Connector feed articles show only a SIEM TCP port; the ZIA NSS overview describes an HTTPS feed type for VM-based NSS, and whether it applies to Cloud & Branch Connector feeds is not stated.

quotes: HTTPS Feed: Uses the TLS protocol to load-balance and encrypt syslog feeds between NSS and your SIEM.
